title: Quantum Bayesian networks with application to games displaying Parrondo’s paradox
abstract_summary: The author reformulates Bayesian networks in terms of linear maps and proposes a natural extension that is shown to be equivalent to standard textbook quantum mechanics, enabling unified models that mix classical and quantum behavior. The dissertation develops quantum Bayesian networks, proves consistency results, and applies the framework to analyze classical and quantum versions of games exhibiting Parrondo’s paradox, deriving bounds on paradoxical behavior and presenting quantum-walk constructions that achieve these bounds.
methodology_description: This work is theoretical and mathematical. The author reformulates classical Bayesian networks as linear maps on spaces of measures and then motivates a natural extension to maps on density-matrix-valued spaces (quantum nodes). The methodology is: (1) set out three modeling principles (positivity of computed probabilities, linearity, and potential universality) and show their implications; (2) develop two concrete technical frameworks to enforce these principles — Option I (measure‑theoretic approach with σ-finite base measures and an atomic variant, including an Option I') and Option II (compact Hausdorff spaces, Borel σ-algebras and weak*‑continuous maps) — and spell out the corresponding admissible map classes and tensor-product rules; (3) define and analyze transition probability functions and pseudo-transition objects for the classical case and their analogues for density-matrix-valued maps; (4) introduce graphical primitives (nodes, splitters, pince-nez, terminators) and a calculus for composing maps in networks; (5) prove foundational results (existence/uniqueness, lifting results, tensor-product density, no-cloning impossibility, embedding results) using tools from measure theory, functional analysis and operator algebras (Radon–Nikodým theorem, spectral theorem for compact operators, Stinespring and Sakai representation theorems, tensor product norm arguments, etc.); (6) show the equivalence of the quantum-node Bayesian-network formalism to standard textbook quantum mechanics under the chosen assumptions; (7) apply the framework to construct and analyze examples (double-slit, teleportation, Bell scenarios) and to formulate and bound Parrondo-like phenomena: (a) define a single-round Parrondo-like game on geodesics of projective Hilbert space, develop metrics (trace and round metrics), characterize geodesics and then derive tight bounds on the possible paradoxical probability values using operator/matrix inequalities and extremal arguments; (b) construct explicit quantum-walk models (via CMV matrices and coined-walk representations) that achieve the derived bounds; (8) collect the general technical supporting results and detailed proofs in extensive appendices. The paper is purely analytic and constructive; results are proven mathematically rather than obtained by numerical experiments.
key_findings: [supported] Bayesian networks / graphical models can be reformulated in terms of linear maps on spaces of measures, and this gives a clean, compositional formulation for probabilistic graphical models.

[supported] Replacing measures with density-matrix-valued spaces (and using completely positive maps) yields a natural extension of Bayesian networks that is mathematically equivalent (under stated conditions) to standard textbook quantum mechanics (Stinespring / CP-map formalism).

[supported] Two implementation options for the formalism are given (Option I: measure-theoretic / L1-based with base measures; Option II: C(X)-based with compact Hausdorff spaces), each with precise technical trade-offs; the paper proves existence/continuity/lifting results for both.
[supported] The framework preserves useful Bayesian-network features (modularity, conditioning/marginalization, splitters/pince-nez) and enables mixed classical–quantum models.

[supported] The classical notions of cloning and teleportation are analyzed: cloning is impossible in Bayesian-network models for essentially the same linearity reasons in both classical-hidden and quantum nodes; teleportation-like behavior can be implemented in purely classical hidden-node constructions as well as quantum constructions (explicit constructions provided).
[supported] There is no general 'quantum Copy' map on density matrices (theorem proving nonexistence).

[supported] Concrete theorems give exact bounds on how extreme a Parrondo-like paradox can be for single-round games when initial states are connected by geodesics in projective Hilbert space; the quantum case has precise attainable bounds and constructions (quantum walks) that saturate them are provided.
[supported] The paper constructs quantum-walk examples (CMV / coined-walk style) that realize the maximum Parrondo-like discrepancy allowed by the derived bounds.

[supported] Many technical functional-analytic supporting results are proved (existence of lifts of conditional probabilities under common conditions, characterization of positive/CP maps, density and tensor-product density results for L1- and C(X)-type spaces, relations between diag maps and trace-class operators, etc.).

[speculative] The author suggests the quantum-extension of Bayesian networks could be useful outside of physics (e.g., weather or finance forecasting) but acknowledges experimental validation is needed.

[speculative] The Bayesian-network presentation is argued to be more flexible and practically convenient than tube-style textbook quantum-circuit representations for mixing classical and quantum elements and for indicating conditioning/marginalization graphically.

[speculative] It is left as an open question whether there exist other linear-space structures (beyond measures and density matrices and their tensor products) suitable for the same compositional, positivity-and-linearity constraints.
results_summary: This dissertation develops a formulation of Bayesian networks as networks of linear maps on spaces of measures and shows a natural, rigorously justified extension obtained by replacing measure spaces with density-matrix-valued spaces and enforcing complete positivity. The extension reproduces textbook quantum mechanics (via standard operator-algebra/Stinespring results) while retaining the modular advantages of Bayesian networks and enabling mixed classical–quantum graphical models. The work proves many supporting functional-analytic results, clarifies conceptual confusions (e.g., no-cloning vs no-copying), constructs classical and quantum teleportation-style protocols, and analyzes Parrondo-type paradoxes: it derives tight bounds for a Parrondo-like effect on single-round games and gives quantum-walk constructions that saturate those bounds.
quantum_advantage_detail: The paper proves (mathematically) that quantum (density-matrix) Bayesian-network models can exhibit behavior (Parrondo-like discrepancies) outside the bounds applicable to classical-hidden models and provides explicit quantum-walk constructions that attain the derived maximal discrepancy. These are theoretical constructions and proofs rather than empirical demonstrations.
limitations: Extending conditional probabilities to general linear maps introduces additional maps and complications beyond standard transition probability functions (author-stated).
Option I' requires a choice of base measures (σ-finite) for each space; this can preclude direct copying and complicates input of continuous parameters (author-stated).
Under Option I' many useful operations (e.g., the Copy map) fail when the base measure has an infinitely-divisible part (author-stated).

Option II requires compact Hausdorff spaces and Borel σ-algebras and restriction to weak*-continuous maps (author-stated); this imposes topological constraints compared to more general measurable settings.
Measurements and conditioning modeled as projective maps (textbook rules) are unnecessary and can force extra arbitrary structure (unitaries, projectors) that complicates modeling (author-stated).
No universal quantum Copy map exists; cloning is impossible in both classical-hidden and quantum Bayesian networks (author-stated).

Embedding quantum models into classical models is necessarily contextual (so a classical embedding is not noncontextual) and, in general, cannot be done via a simple base-measure L1 embedding (Theorem 3.5.2) (author-stated).
Embedding classical models into quantum ones requires diagonal embedding and fails for measures with an infinitely-divisible part (author-stated).
Complete-positive (CP) maps form a convex cone that, in infinite dimensions, has no interior — this raises issues for approximation and numerical methods (author-stated).

Lifting conditional probabilities to transition probability functions is not always straightforward; only certain standard conditions guarantee a lift (e.g., standard Borel spaces or countable atoms) (author-stated).
No infinite-dimensional analogue of Lebesgue measure impedes a direct extension of the classical approximation approach to field theories (author-stated).

Several existence proofs and structural results rely on nonconstructive theorems (e.g., transfinite induction, Sakai, Stinespring) and the axiom of choice, so practical constructive procedures may be missing (author-stated).

The meaning of 'teleportation' in the Bayesian-network sense can differ from colloquial/operational interpretations; classical analogues can mimic some aspects, blurring conceptual clarity (author-stated).
[inferred] Scalability concerns: operator and map dimensions grow rapidly (operators ~ n^2, maps ~ n^4), suggesting computational blow-up for large systems and many particles.
[inferred] Practical numerical construction and stable approximation of CP maps, Stinespring dilations, and lifts are non-unique and may be fragile for implementations.
[inferred] The approaches place model-building burden on users (choice of option I' vs II, base measures, auxiliary spaces), which complicates adoption in applied domains such as finance.

[inferred] Restrictions to compact or metric spaces (option II) and to σ-finite base measures (option I') limit the direct applicability to some real-world datasets and continuous-parameter models common in finance.

#idea:hybrid-approach — The formalism naturally supports mixed classical–quantum graphical models (classical measure-nodes and quantum density-nodes) preserving Bayesian-network modularity, conditioning and marginalization, offering a compositional approach to combine classical and quantum components.
